question: Is my HeartBug data private?
aliases: who has access to my data
short_answer: Yes. Your recordings are encrypted and protected, and only HeartBug’s clinical team and your doctor can access them. Your data is not shared without your permission.
long_answer: Your data is handled under strict Australian privacy principles and industry-standard clinical security practices. Your recordings are encrypted and securely transferred. All information is encrypted, access-controlled, and protected at every stage. Only HeartBug’s clinical team and your doctor have access to your data, and it is never shared without your permission.

question: Is my health data securely stored?
short_answer: Yes. Your heart data is stored in secure, encrypted medical systems that meet Australian healthcare standards.
long_answer: Your heart data and health information are stored in secure, encrypted medical systems that meet Australian healthcare data-protection standards.

question: What kind of data does HeartBug collect?
short_answer: HeartBug collects ECG recordings, your symptom notes, technical monitoring data, and basic identification details. It does not collect audio, photos, contacts, or other phone data.
long_answer: HeartBug only collects your heart’s electrical activity (ECG), your symptom notes, technical information needed for monitoring, and your identification information. We do not collect audio, photos, contacts, or personal phone data.

question: Does HeartBug record my voice or conversations?
short_answer: No. The device never records audio. The app only uses the microphone while you use the voice feature, and no audio is saved.
long_answer: The HeartBug device itself never records your voice or conversations. It only captures your heart’s electrical activity. When you talk to me inside the app, your phone’s microphone listens so I can understand you, and some background sound may be heard during that moment — but nothing is saved or stored. The microphone is only active while you're using the voice feature, and HeartBug does not record or keep any audio at any time.

question: Does HeartBug track my GPS location?
short_answer: No. HeartBug does not use GPS and does not record your location.
long_answer: HeartBug does not use GPS and does not collect or record your location at any time.

question: How do I contact HeartBug?
short_answer: Call 1800 529 275 or email patientcare@heartbug.com.au during business hours (Sydney time).
long_answer: You can reach HeartBug on 1800 529 275 or by emailing patientcare@heartbug.com.au. Support is available during business hours (Sydney time).

question: Who can see my HeartBug heart data?
short_answer: Only your treating doctor and authorised HeartBug clinical staff can access your recordings and report, unless required by law or you give written consent.
long_answer: Only your treating doctor and authorised HeartBug clinical staff can access your recordings and reports. No one else — including third parties, family members, marketers, insurers, employers, researchers, or other organisations — can access your data unless required by law or with your explicit written consent.

question: Does HeartBug sell or use my data for advertising?
short_answer: No. HeartBug does not sell, rent, or use your data for advertising or marketing.
long_answer: HeartBug does not sell, rent, or use your data for advertising, marketing, or commercial targeting.

question: Can I request my data to be deleted?
short_answer: You can request access to your data, but medical records can’t always be deleted due to legal requirements. Requests must be in writing to patientcare@heartbug.com.au.
long_answer: You may request access to your data, but medical records cannot always be deleted due to legal clinical-documentation requirements. HeartBug can guide you through the process. The request needs to be in writing and emailed to patientcare@heartbug.com.au.

question: What happens if there is a data breach?
short_answer: HeartBug follows strict security protocols. If a breach occurred, it would be handled under Australian breach notification laws and you and your doctor/clinic would be informed promptly.
long_answer: HeartBug has strict security protocols to prevent breaches. If an incident did occur, it would be managed under Australian data-breach notification laws, and you, your clinic, and your doctor would be contacted immediately.

question: What are HeartBug’s operating hours?
short_answer: Support is available Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm Sydney time. Outside hours, leave a message or email; for emergencies call 000.
long_answer: HeartBug support is available Monday to Friday, 9am–5pm (Sydney time). Messages received outside these hours will be responded to as soon as possible during business hours. If it is a medical concern, contact your doctor or call 000 in an emergency.

question: Who do I contact for medical concerns or symptoms?
aliases: who to call for health issues
short_answer: Contact your doctor for medical concerns. HeartBug support helps only with device/monitoring issues. Call 000 for emergencies.
long_answer: For any medical concerns or questions about your symptoms, please contact your doctor directly. HeartBug support can assist with device and monitoring issues only. HeartBug is not an emergency service; if you are feeling unwell or it is an emergency, call 000 immediately.

question: Is my data deleted after monitoring ends?
short_answer: Recordings are removed from the device after upload, but remain securely stored on HeartBug servers as required for medical records.
long_answer: Your data is removed from the device once it uploads, but remains securely stored on HeartBug’s encrypted servers for clinical and medical record purposes even after monitoring, as required by law.

question: Does HeartBug comply with privacy laws?
short_answer: Yes. HeartBug complies with the Australian Privacy Act 1988 and medical data protection requirements.
long_answer: HeartBug complies fully with the Australian Privacy Act 1988 and all medical data protection requirements.
